beur-hagra/1:א: (א) Seif 1 and blesses. As written in Eruvin 40b and Avodah Zarah:
beur-hagra/1:ב: (ב) And if it falls on Shabbat. See Tosafot Pesachim 106a s.v. zokhreihu, etc.:
beur-hagra/1:ד: (ד) And if he forgot. For havdalah requires a cup, as written there and in chapter 8 of Berachot; and the one who blesses must taste, as written in chapter erev Pesach and chapter 8 of Berachot; and since he began the Haggadah it is forbidden to drink, as written between the cups, etc., and as Ramban wrote in Milchamot and Ran, unlike Razah there; and Tosafot 103b s.v. Rav Ashi:
beur-hagra/1:ה: (ה) And one does not, etc., and if. See Tosafot Chagigah 18b s.v. hanotel, etc., and he wrote "and one should not bless," etc.:
beur-hagra/1:ו: (ו) And for a common person. And so one infers the language in the Mishnah: "they poured for him the first cup," and so in all:
beur-hagra/2:_: Seif 2 and he does not. See siman 474 from what is written:
beur-hagra/3:_: Seif 3 and nevertheless. Yerushalmi there: why — lest he become drunk? He is already drunk! What is the difference between wine within the meal and wine after the meal? Wine after the meal intoxicates; wine within the meal does not intoxicate. And since he did not challenge from before the meal, learn that before too it intoxicates, only it is not customary to drink much before eating:
beur-hagra/4:א: (א) Seif 4 they bring before a common person. There 115b, and the halachah is like R. Huna:
beur-hagra/4:ב: (ב) Bowl. See Tosafot there s.v. lamah:
beur-hagra/4:ג: (3) Three. Kmash in blessings 39 2 and Shabbat 17 2 everything is acknowledged on Pesach 20 and in siman 20 what is the poor of his way in a slice 20 and there is another B. Shalimot for the Mishnah bread Kmash there and there everything is thanked on Shabbat 20 and the 5th 19th of the Leviticus there was no Gach coming down from the Kmash the Rif in P. AP and also Amarinan in Rish 19 2 2 and it was on the sixth day 20 Prepares for Shabbat Chul prepares 19 20 and Esi' 129 SA and it is the opinion of the Rabbi at the end of Passovers and SAF and Mordechai but the opinion of the Rabbi 5 AP and the Rambam in the Ph.h. Henceforth it is not a way of poverty, since there are two matzos, and also one half matzah, but as above, and the one who brings out the bread blesses the slice, and both are performed, and it is not like making matzot packages, since it is like a matzoh, there is everything. And packages 20 and 24 of the Rashba will not be called in the answer, as well as the main point:
beur-hagra/4:ד: (ד) Matzah and maror, etc. Mishnah there:
beur-hagra/4:ה: (ה) And karpas or, etc. There: "they brought before him" — he dips, etc.; and Ran wrote when there are no other vegetables, and as written in the Gemara there; and see Magen Avraham:
beur-hagra/4:ו: (ו) And vinegar or. Mishnah there: he dips in chazeret; and see Tosafot there s.v. matbil, etc.:
beur-hagra/4:ט: (ט) Custom, etc., and the meat custom, etc. Like Ravina there; and Ran wrote he disagrees with all; and see Ran; and there 116b "this meat," etc.; and custom is egg in place of cooking; and Kol Bo wrote in the name of Yerushalmi they were accustomed to shank and egg; and see Beit Yosef:
beur-hagra/4:י: (י) And he arranges, etc. As written in chapter 3 of Yoma 32b; and see Tosafot there s.v. avurei and Mefareish, etc.:
beur-hagra/4:כ: (כ) Custom, etc., and the egg. Per R. Yitzchak in Tosafot there s.v. shnei, and as stam Mishnah — these matters are not like ben Teima; and so Rambam:
beur-hagra/4:ל: (ל) On coals. As written there 75a: "he cut it," etc.; and in Beitza one cannot, for it requires a pomegranate skewer:
beur-hagra/4:מ: (מ) And likewise roasted. Like ben Teima, for stam Mishnah of erev Pesach is like him, as written in chapter 6 there; and as Tosafot wrote there and there:
beur-hagra/5:א: (א) Seif 5 but not. Since it taught only stalk:
beur-hagra/5:ב: (ב) And if there is none. As written there: "but chazeret we learned" — learn that he was particular about order:
beur-hagra/5:ג: (ג) And if there is none. Like Rav Huna there who ruled like the others:
beur-hagra/5:ד: (ד) And charoset, etc., and afterward. There 116a: therefore one needs, etc.:
beur-hagra/5:ו: (ו) And they make. As written there: remembrance of tapuach; and Geonim explained see there that Israel are compared to this apple, etc.:
beur-hagra/5:ז: (ז) And they place on it, etc. There: spices, etc.:
beur-hagra/6:ב: (ב) And he should not bless. See Tosafot there s.v. kol, etc.; and see siman 158 seif 4 that the essence is he should bless on netilat yadayim for something dipped in liquid — see there:
beur-hagra/6:ג: (ג) And he takes. Mishnah: he dips in chazeret, etc., as above:
beur-hagra/6:ד: (ד) Less than a kezayit. Since he takes only for recognition, and they bless on less than a kezayit, as Tosafot wrote chapter 2 of Sukkah in the name of Yerushalmi, and as written in chapter 6 of Berachot; and one should not take a kezayit; and see Taz:
beur-hagra/6:ו: (ו) And he does not bless afterward. Meaning even if he ate a kezayit, as above; and it is from what is written 115a at first, etc., without a berachah — thus the first berachah exempts it; and see Rashbam 114b s.v. peshita, etc.; and see Tosafot 115a s.v. vehadar, etc., who disagree with Rashbam, and R. Yitzchak Tov Elem; but Rosh there explains like Rashbam; and Tosafot's question is from what is written 115b in the aggadah that Hallel was an interruption specifically for netilat yadayim but not for berachah, for even companions who removed [the table] it was not an interruption when they left some companions; and see Tosafot 102a s.v. ve'akru, etc.; and it is written in Seder HaPesach that the difference of these explanations is for birkat hamazon; and see Tosafot 100b s.v. yedei yayin, etc.; and it appears they follow their view and the dispute in siman 474; and see Rosh there sk 24; and it appears to me, etc., that it is different in birkat hamazon, etc., but if he stood, etc.; and see Tosafot 103b s.v. Rav; and if you ask, etc., and per my explanation, etc.; and see Ran; and so Taz; and therefore Shulchan Aruch ruled well according to his view, but according to Rabbenu Yonah there too one must bless:
beur-hagra/6:ז: (ז) And he takes matzah. As above: what is the relevance, etc.; and he said the middle one, as written in Berachot and Shabbat there — a piece within the whole; and see what I wrote there's help:
beur-hagra/6:ח: (ח) And he places half. That both eatings that he eats for the sake of matzah should be from the piece:
beur-hagra/6:ט: (ט) And he raises. As written: matzah requires raising; and see Hagahot Maimonides end of Laws of Monetary Damages see there:
beur-hagra/6:י: (י) And he says in the language, etc. As written: "and you shall tell," etc.:
beur-hagra/6:כ: (כ) And then he commands. There: why do they remove, etc.; and see Tosafot there s.v. lamah, etc.:
beur-hagra/7:א: (א) Seif 7 immediately. Meaning after removing the bowl immediately, so that they will ask; and as written above; and here the son asks, etc.; and as written:
beur-hagra/7:ב: (ב) If there is none. Gemara there:
beur-hagra/7:ג: (ג) And when the son. There 115-116: he dismisses them, etc.:
beur-hagra/7:ד: (ד) And when he begins, etc. See Tosafot 114a s.v. hevi'u, etc.:
beur-hagra/7:ה: (ה) And when he reaches "therefore." Midrash Shir HaShirim; and he said there in order to say song over the wine, as written in Arachin 11a; and Hallel is the song, as written there 10b and chapter 4 of Rosh Hashanah and chapter 1 of Megillah:
beur-hagra/7:ו: (ו) And custom is to sprinkle. As written in Yerushalmi beginning chapter erev Pesach: from where four cups, etc.; and the Sages said corresponding to the four cups of punishment that the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to give, etc. — see there:
beur-hagra/7:ז: (ז) With his finger. See there: "it is the finger of the Almighty:"
beur-hagra/7:ט: (ט) And the bread shall be, etc. As written there they answer him words:
beur-hagra/7:י: (י) And then, etc. As written above 102: "and if he brought," etc.; and Rosh wrote there, in the name of Yerushalmi: because of his shame that he is earlier in the verse and earlier for berachah:
chok-yaakov/1:א: (א) And he blesses Shehecheyanu. And if he did not say it on day one he blesses on day two or on one of the other days when he remembers; and if he has no cup of wine at the time of Kiddush he blesses shehecheyanu without a cup — Riaz in Shaarei Geulah chapter 2 of every erev; and so Magen Avraham, and it is simple in the Gemara chapter Lulav and Aravah, and similarly explained in Laws of Chanukah siman 677 see there; and Magen Avraham further wrote, and it appears to me the same if he forgot to say shehecheyanu on the second night he blesses all seven — end quote; and it appears the same for Shavuot, even though only two days, nevertheless it has make-up all seven. And further it appears simple that if he forgot to say shehecheyanu on the first night and on the second night said shehecheyanu, he need not say shehecheyanu again based on the first night to complete — for if the first day is holy he completed shehecheyanu on the second day, and if the second day is holy behold he said shehecheyanu; and if he forgot to say Kiddush at night his law is as above siman 471 seif 8, and so Eliyah Rabbah below seif 485; and if he forgot to say the Haggadah it is obvious he has no make-up at all, as written "because of this" when matzah and maror are before you, and so Magen Avraham below siman 485; and he challenged Eliyah Rabbah on this, that he understood in his words it refers to the Haggadah, and this is not so — he only wrote the law if he forgot Kiddush, as written:
chok-yaakov/1:ב: (ב) Shehecheyanu and they do not say "who performed miracles for us" because he will say it in the Haggadah — so Tur and Maharil; Maharil wrote another reason see there; and Rokeach and Agudah wrote — all is in it: that they do not say the berachah "who commanded us to drink four cups" because each is a mitzvah by itself and there is interruption:
chok-yaakov/1:ג: (ג) And if it falls on Shabbat. It is permitted to say the Haggadah on Pesach even alone, and we are not concerned he will lean, as explained above siman 471 seif 9, and not like the view of Maharil siman 193 who forbids:
chok-yaakov/1:ד: (ד) He says Yekum Purkan. And they do not bless on spices every motzei Shabbat for Yom Tov, and many reasons were said — see in Tosafot and Rosh chapter erev Pesach; and Magen Avraham wrote they say havdalah seated like Kiddush, and so is custom to recline; and it appears to me the reason as explained above siman 322 that Hallel they say only standing; nevertheless on Pesach night they say it reclining, in the way of reclining and freedom — if so, the same for Kiddush and havdalah; and not like one who wrote one should stand when it falls on Shabbat, as written:
chok-yaakov/1:ה: (ה) He completes the Haggadah. Levush wrote: "and he should not interrupt the Haggadah" — it implies the reason is it is forbidden to interrupt during the Haggadah; but this I did not find in any posek, and also why should he not interrupt in telling the Haggadah for the mitzvah of havdalah (and see above siman 472 sk 2), especially between sections; rather it appears to me the reason is simple: havdalah requires a cup; if he makes havdalah during saying the Haggadah he will interrupt afterward between havdalah and the berachah on the cup with saying the Haggadah; and it is better he bless on the cup and pour another cup for saying the Haggadah, because this appears like adding to the cup since he took a fixed cup for havdalah; and since it is possible in another way we act accordingly; and see in seif 3:
chok-yaakov/1:ו: (ו) And afterward he makes havdalah. And Magen Avraham wrote: and if he remembered in the middle of his meal that he had not made havdalah, he makes havdalah immediately on the cup and recites borei peri hagafen if he did not have in mind to drink wine during the meal; and he should not wait to make havdalah until after the meal, for that is like adding to the cups, for one may not say havdalah and Hallel on one cup. And if he forgot until after Birkat HaMazon, he says Hallel and havdalah on one cup, since it is impossible otherwise — end of his words, Magen Avraham; and see there siman 496.
chok-yaakov/1:ז: (ז) And one should not wash the hands at all before kiddush. Behold, the later authorities multiplied opinions on this; and in my humble opinion the essential ruling follows the Mechaber's decision, and so agreed the Taz — that one who sees him washing his hands will think he also recites al netilat yadayim as during the rest of the year; but in truth it is forbidden to recite a berakha, since this washing is not for eating matzah, for it is a great interruption.
chok-yaakov/1:ח: (ח) He should not pour for himself. This too is the Mechaber's intent in what he wrote in his wording: and they pour for him through others.
chok-yaakov/2:_: He drinks reclining. And if he drank without reclining, see there siman 472 seif 7 and what is written there.
chok-yaakov/3:א: (א) Permission is in his hand. According to what the Mechaber wrote below siman 474 in the gloss — that our custom is to recite a first berakha on each and every cup, which is not per the Rash's view — if so, that which is permitted to drink between the cups is specifically when he had it in mind in a manner that he need not recite borei peri hagafen on it; otherwise it is like adding to the cups, as the Tur wrote in the name of R' Meir of Rothenburg, and so is the Bach's conclusion even per the Rash's view — see there.
chok-yaakov/3:ב: (ב) So that he not become intoxicated. And according to this it implies that other beverages that are not intoxicating are permitted to drink; however, according to what the Mordekhai wrote — the reason that between the first and second it is permitted to drink is that wine whets the appetite and he will eat matzah with appetite — it is possible that other beverages are forbidden to drink between the first and second, since they do not whet; however, we have not found any posek who had a concern of prohibition in this, only regarding wine it was necessary to permit it so it not be like adding to the cups, and also so you not say "wine satisfies, satisfies"; and see there siman 471.
chok-yaakov/4:א: (א) And karpas. Or another vegetable — meaning that it is eaten raw and cooked, on which one recites borei peri ha-adamah, as above siman 200; and the custom is to take what they call parsley; and it is good to take karpas, which is a notarikon: sixty ten thousands did arduous labor, and they call it in foreign tongue eppich; and so wrote the later authorities.
chok-yaakov/4:ב: (ב) Or salt water. And if Pesach falls on Shabbat, he should make the salt water on erev Shabbat; and if he did not make it on erev Shabbat and he has no vinegar, he should make a little salt water, as explained above siman 321.
chok-yaakov/4:ג: (ג) And one in remembrance of the festival offering. Even if Pesach falls on Shabbat, the Tur also concludes that he takes two cooked dishes, not per the Rash's view; and it requires study, for in the Rash's abridged rulings he copied that one takes two cooked dishes even on the first day of Yom Tov, while the Rash's view there is actually the opposite.
chok-yaakov/4:ד: (ד) In remembrance of the festival offering: And the Rokeach wrote: there are those who say that one takes two cooked dishes in remembrance of Moshe and Aharon.
chok-yaakov/4:ה: (ה) And charoset. And they should be closer. In the Shulchan Aruch it is printed here in the name of Maharil, but in truth in Maharil I did not find this; rather he wrote, and these are his words: the eppich vegetable is fit to place so it be closer to it than the matzot, for if the matzot were close he would not need to break the afikoman from the first one so as not to pass over the matzot — end of his words. But charoset, meat, and egg were not mentioned at all, since one does not recite a berakha on them but only brings them on the table as a mere remembrance — the rule of not passing over the matzot does not apply to them at all. And there is one who says charoset is not a mitzvah, as in the mishnah in the chapter Arvei Pesachim; and Maharil was particular only regarding matzah, which is a mitzvah on which one recites a berakha and which we were commanded, and it is also prior in the order of berakhot — therefore one should be particular to bring the vegetables closer to him than the dishes; and even maror was not mentioned at all in Maharil to distance or bring close, even though one recites a berakha on it and was commanded; and it is possible that since it is not beloved to a person and has no precedence law in berakhot, Maharil was not particular about maror. Also the proof from the western lamp that Maharil brought there — one may distinguish; see there.
chok-yaakov/4:ו: (ו) And likewise roasted. And they eat it because it is a remembrance of mourning, as explained below siman 476; and the roasted meat one does not eat — and such is the custom — even in a place where they were accustomed to eat other roasted foods, because it is a remembrance of the Pesach offering; (and so is the Taz's conclusion, that this is the essential ruling). And if he forgot to roast the meat or the egg on erev Yom Tov, he should not roast at night unless he had in mind to eat it that night and day (Mahari"v siman 193).
chok-yaakov/5:א: (א) Lettuce (chazeret). Since not everyone is expert in them and their names, and the language also changes according to countries, and not all vegetables are found in every place — therefore I said to copy here all the explanations of these vegetables as I found among the poskim, so that each person according to his language and country may understand the matter clearly. Chazeret is explained in the Gemara in Pesachim that it is chasa (lettuce); Rashi: latugi; the Arukh: latok; in Hagahot Maimoniot: lettuce or latukh; the Levush wrote that it is what we call in these countries zarzich; and the Mechaber's brother in Sha'ar HaTziyon wrote in the name of "I found written" that he challenged the Levush on this — only that it is called in foreign tongue latukh, and in Romance lektuka; and in medical books seven types are found from it — and there is no connection at all to zarzich found in these countries — end of his words. And in Berakhot chapter HaRo'eh regarding Bar Hedya interpreting dreams: "tired are your affairs like lettuce" — Rashi: that it is doubled and thick; and I heard from a foreigner that in a hot foreign land lettuce is found in Nissan days and is doubled and thick like what we call in these countries latif in foreign tongue, and they eat it — this is the species for maror. And see in Beit Yosef that he wrote: the mitzvah is with chazeret even though it is sweet and has no bitterness — therefore; and see there in chapter HaRo'eh regarding Bar Hedya, who said to Rava: your affair is bitter — it must be that nevertheless it has some bitterness. And in the Arukh: chazeret galin is bitter lettuce. And in the Agudah: if latugi is not found, take maraytikh — end of his words. Olashin in the Gemara: hindbi; Rashi: krishfla; the Arukh: olashin that satisfy; in foreign tongue sintzoni; and some say krispinyo — end of his words. And in Shulchan Shel Maharil I found that it was estrula; and some say in foreign tongue amatika andibi; and so Ra'avad — it is andibi, and it is found among us that they cook it and eat it with sugar and vinegar to nullify the bitterness. In Hagahot Maimoniot it is korvil, also found among us; but in Maharil, since in the siddurim it says to take korvil for the first dipping, it implies one does not fulfill maror with it. Tamcha — Rashi: marubya; Arukh: kardoya mariyo; later authorities wrote it is what they call in foreign tongue krien or maertikh; and so Tosefet Yom Tov; and see there what he challenged on Ra'avad; and so the custom spread in these countries to take krien for maror and to recite the berakha on the leaves, and for korekh they take the stalk. Charchevina is in the Gemara: atzvata dedikla; Rashi: videlah; Rokeach: agroryin. Maror in the Gemara: mararita; Rashi: amirfoyil in Poritz; Agudah: vermut, meaning wormwood.
chok-yaakov/5:ב: (ב) Unless they are moist. It implies that even if they are not completely dry, only wilted, one does not fulfill with them since they are not so moist — so Ri'az in Shibolei HaLeket; and so is the implication of most poskim, and so in Kol Bo. And that which the Gemara says one fulfills with wilted — it refers to stalks, as the Gemara concludes; and with stalks, since we hold one fulfills with dry, all the more so with wilted one fulfills according to his view; and although this is very obvious, I wrote it because Magen Avraham wrote on that which stalks fulfill whether moist — it implies one does not fulfill with wilted, and so implies Tur and Rambam — end of his words; and it is a printing error, an error that is evident, and it refers to leaves, as written; and see there siman 336 whether if one buries them in earth from before Yom Tov so they not wilt, it is permitted to take them — see there.
chok-yaakov/5:ג: (ג) But not pickled. Rashi explains: in vinegar; and the later authorities wrote that Rashi follows his view, as Beit Yosef wrote in Yoreh De'ah siman 105 in his name — that pickling in water alone is not pickling, only in vinegar and brine; but we hold that something soaked in water from the eve is considered pickled like cooked — therefore they wrote one should protest those who soak maror and leave it so from the eve, for one does not fulfill with it. And in my humble opinion it appears that the custom of Israel is Torah (that they soak it so the leaves be moist and not wilted, as in s"k 19), and they have support — for even to the poskim regarding prohibition of being pickled in water from the eve, for absorption and expulsion — nevertheless here they agree that specifically in vinegar it becomes pickled, as the Gemara says there daf 39: this marorita — the general rule: anything that has bitter taste one fulfills with; anything not pickled in vinegar still has bitter taste; and so the matter appears to the eye and senses. Proof: the mishnah and braita there teach: but not pickled, not scalded, not cooked; Tosafot there: not scalded and not cooked implies scalding is more than cooking — if not so it would be "this and all the more so this," and so in many places — end of Tosafot; and so agreed the poskim. Still a difficulty: at least it should be "this and all the more so this" at the beginning — "but not pickled," which is less than cooking, and all the more so scalding and cooking; at the end "but not scalded and not cooked" should be "not this nor this," since scalding is more than cooking. Rather certainly this pickling refers to pickling in vinegar, per Rashi; and vinegar changes and nullifies bitterness more than scalding and cooking in water. If so, the whole mishnah is brought in one category by way of "not this nor this"; and now the general rule: to include pickling in water, since it retains bitter taste one fulfills — except per every rule I wrote in my book Ma'aseh Yesharim — many poskim hold no pickling law in water from the eve; even though for prohibition we are stringent, nevertheless for maror nowadays, which is rabbinic, it is also a stringency that leads to leniency that they eat when wilted; also we do not find in any early posek who wrote for prohibition in pickling in water — there is clear proof to permit; therefore one should not be stringent as above; and so one may say below siman 521 — see there.
chok-yaakov/5:ד: (ד) Combine to a kezayit. Which is like half an egg of a hen; and this measure is required in completeness, apart from the space between the leaves, as stated below siman 486; and one should be careful in this, for otherwise it is a berakha in vain, since he recites a berakha on eating and eating implies a kezayit. One who is ill or a nauseous person may take for himself whichever maror species is less bitter for him; and if he cannot at all, at least he eats a little or chews in his mouth to remember the taste of bitterness without a berakha; and it is fit to exert himself with all his ability even if it pains him, to fulfill the mitzvah of the Sages, as written siman 472 s"k 22 — see there.
chok-yaakov/5:ה: (ה) And the essential mitzvah is with chazeret, and Beit Yosef wrote in the name of Semak: even to buy at expensive prices — meaning up to a third of the mitzvah; see in Magen Avraham what he wrote in the name of Mahari"v; and whether a Jew may cut the maror himself — see above siman 494 s"k 7.
chok-yaakov/5:ו: (ו) Wormwood. See there s"k 18 that I wrote in the name of the Agudah that this is the maror mentioned in the Gemara.
chok-yaakov/5:ז: (ז) Or another bitter vegetable. Nevertheless, even though it is impossible otherwise, at least one should not recite a berakha except on these species enumerated in the mishnah, since it teaches "these vegetables"; and so is the implication of all poskim — specifically these; and so agreed Shach and Magen Avraham.
chok-yaakov/5:ח: (ח) And charoset. He should make it thick; Rokeach siman 266: and they make charoset on the sixth day, or if he wishes on erev Yom Tov which is Yom Tov, permission is in his hand, as in chapter Arvei Pesachim daf 117 — charoset is a mitzvah and not a preparatory mitzvah — end of his words. That which he ruled charoset is a mitzvah is in remembrance of clay and blood, as the Mechaber wrote, and per the Rash in chapter Arvei Pesachim, and so Rambam in his book, and Tur siman 475; nevertheless one does not recite a berakha on it, since it is subordinate to maror, as Tur wrote in siman 472 — unlike the implication of Rambam in his mishnah commentary; see Bach siman 471. And great wonder on the Levush, who in siman 471 seif 2 ruled plainly that charoset is not a mitzvah at all, while in this siman and in siman 475 ruled the opposite, as those who say it is a mitzvah — it requires study.
chok-yaakov/5:ט: (ט) A little vinegar. Agudah's wording: and on the table one grinds it; and if Pesach occurs on Shabbat, he must put the liquid in it from erev Shabbat; and if he forgot, he may do it through a change — meaning he puts the liquid first in the vessel and afterward puts the charoset in it, as explained above siman 328 seif 16; and so Magen Avraham; and see Taz s"k 10, who forbids putting baked matzah meal to mix with wine or honey water on Shabbat even through a change — his words are not compelling; also the world is not careful about this.
chok-yaakov/5:י: (י) Similar to straw. And one should not grind them well so they be long. Beit Yosef.
chok-yaakov/6:א: (א) He washes the hands. Taz wrote: from here there is open reproof to those not careful all year to wash hands for things dipped in liquid; and if one comes to purify himself more on this night, at least he should be careful also on days of repentance — only here there is lack of vigilance and they do not precisely align their measures — end of his words. HaLevush in chapter 25 wrote: the world is accustomed not to wash and they have support — Tosafot hold so — end of his words; and this is the view of Maharam of Rothenburg that the Tur brought here (and Shakh challenged Maharam in vain); and so Magen Avraham siman 188. And that they wash on this night is like one of the other changes made this night so they will ask.
chok-yaakov/6:ב: (ב) And he does not recite a berakha after it. Even though he ate a kezayit — Bach wrote: it appears one who wishes to fulfill the obligation according to all geonim should eat a full kezayit in this first dipping, and have in mind at borei peri ha-adamah not to exempt maror with this berakha; thereby he is obligated to recite after the first dipping al achilat sh'ar — according to his view; and afterward when he recites ha-motzi he should also intend not to exempt maror with ha-motzi, and return to recite borei peri ha-adamah on maror and al achilat sh'ar — then he fulfills all views, and there is no unnecessary berakha since he does so to remove himself from dispute — end of his words. Still he does not fulfill according to Semag siman 220, that one does not recite on maror since he does not come to enjoy but only as a remembrance; therefore it appears to me the essential ruling is as most early authorities and Maharil siman 59 and Magen Avraham — not to recite at all.
chok-yaakov/6:ג: (ג) And he gives half. Later authorities wrote: meaning the majority of the matzah.
chok-yaakov/6:ד: (ד) And he lifts the plate with everything on it; and some are accustomed to place the afikoman bundle in the cloth on their shoulders in remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt. Peri Megadim siman 245: it is proper to lift the plate in one hand and the matzah in the other and say Ha Lachma Anya, etc. — end of his words.
chok-yaakov/6:ה: (ה) Ha Lachma Anya. And some say Ha Kolachma — see Magen Avraham; Maharshal siman 88: to say it in a loud voice.
chok-yaakov/6:ו: (ו) He commands to remove them. Magen Avraham wrote: now they are not accustomed to remove them — therefore; and some are accustomed to say the plate should be removed even though they do not remove; Peri Megadim siman 249: men of action open the door when saying Kol Dikhfin — if the door is closed how will they come — end of his words; Ra'avan wrote it refers to household members, not others who would come.
chok-yaakov/7:א: (1) Immediately a second cup. And Katha from the Rashel in the response, the sign of 15 and 15 is washing and washing, as they practice, and the cup is not held in his hand until he reaches the Rabbi in his hand, and in siman 20, a model when he says the Passover, and she who stood for our ancestors and for us, and the Omnipresent saves us from them, he will hold the cup in his hand, and then the cup will be covered when he holds the cup in his hand:
chok-yaakov/7:ב: (ב) Mah Nishtanah. Maharil wrote: one says it in a fine melody to praise the Blessed Name; and if erev Pesach is Shabbat, they hurry in everything to eat the afikoman before midnight and that the children not sleep, for they must then remain through the night before beginning kiddush — end of his words; Shlah wrote one should not say the Hagadah reclining but in awe and fear — end of his words; and when saying "and we shall say before Him shirah," say venomar with segol vowel, past tense — for future redemption one does not say shirah, which is feminine, as in the midrash. Agreement of later authorities.
chok-yaakov/7:ג: (ג) And likewise when reaching maror. Unlike when reaching the Pesach our fathers had — he should not hold it in his hand, for it is like raising consecrated items outside; but nevertheless he should look at it. Mahari"v siman 193.
chok-yaakov/7:ד: (4) with his finger 20 in the glossary of customs, throw a dish with the little finger, that is, the pinky, and in the MA 20 a dish to throw with the ring finger, which is in the little one's hand, it is appropriate to collect a dabakmitza hit, and in the DM 20 a dish to take with the finger, just a reminder of what is said, the finger of the Omnipresent is, and also the main thing, and in the Pesach, the sign of Rasa's dish, the pourer of the wine and the washer of the other cup that they throw from it with their finger and squeeze their hands together in order not to drink, which is remembered The name of the beatings and he also dipped his finger in it and was fed up with it, and in these countries there is no practice like this and there is no way to change it if not that it is the most abstinent and there is an eating loss in it because of the sign of KA'A and the custom was not mentioned in any of the first rulings:
chok-yaakov/7:ה: (ה) While saying the Hagadah. Maharil: the matzot should be covered until beginning Avadim — then he reveals them a little from above, to fulfill lechem oni that they answer upon it; also one should not place any matzah on the table besides the three matzot until after finishing the seder, otherwise how is lifting the plate considered lifting the table — end of his words. "Until after the seder" is not precise, for when beginning Avadim he returns the plate to its place and then may place other matzot on it too.
chok-yaakov/7:ו: (ו) Who says the Hagadah. See Beit Yosef that a blind person is also obligated in reading the Hagadah, unlike Ri'az and responsum Radbaz siman 59; and so is the Gemara's conclusion in Pesachim daf 115 — obligated in Hagadah and can discharge others; see Sha'ar Efraim siman 27 who resolves Ri'az's words; nevertheless for practical law he agrees with Beit Yosef's conclusion; still it appears to me when reaching "this matzah" and "this maror" he should say "this," as the Gemara says there — "this" comes to exclude the blind — it implies he should recognize it by sight, as Rashbam explained there; even though per the conclusion there one may distinguish — nevertheless one may say in short formula "matzah that we eat," etc.; see Bach siman 464, who wrote in the name of Maharshal about one who was imprisoned and did not know Hagadah but had a humash and said all parashiyot of the Exodus — end of his words.
chok-yaakov/7:ז: (ז) The cup in his hand. In the text of the berakha Asher Ga'alanu, Mahari"v wrote: when Pesach falls on the first day of Yom Tov, reverse and say first from the Pesach offerings and then from the sacrifices; on the second night the opposite; Peri Megadim siman 261: say everything in one formula from sacrifices and Pesach offerings; agreement of later authorities like Mahari"v.
peri-megadim/1:_: And there is no Taz: Beit Yosef understood that Mordechai refers to the first dipping — that if he washes hands before Kiddush and blesses al netilat yadayim, he will need at the first dipping of vegetables in salt water to wash again, and the berachah of al netilat yadayim of the first [washing] will be in vain because of the interruption; and therefore Beit Yosef wondered, for Kiddush alone is not an interruption as on other days of the year. And Taz explained that Mordechai refers to the second dipping — maror in charoset — and it is not specifically the second dipping but rather it refers to HaMotzi, for he needed to wash again and bless al netilat yadayim for HaMotzi, for the Haggadah is an interruption and the first berachah is in vain; and the language of the Gemara Pesachim 116b holds as Tosafot wrote there s.v. tzarich. And that which Mordechai wrote "because he needs," etc. — emend and it is fitting that it should read: because for this reason he needs to wash hands at the second dipping even though he washed at the first dipping, for the Haggadah is an interruption; all the more so if he washes before Kiddush it is obvious there is interruption and he will need to wash again for the second dipping and for HaMotzi. Or one must emend and the reading is: even though if he washes before Kiddush he will still need to wash for dipping 2 and for HaMotzi, etc.; and see N'tziv who explained like Taz. And that which N'tziv wrote there that Mordechai holds for dipping in liquid one need not bless al netilat yadayim — one can explain likewise, but since Kiddush is an interruption on Pesach according to Beit Yosef's explanation in Mordechai, therefore berachah 1 of al netilat yadayim was in vain and by necessity he must afterward bless a second time al netilat yadayim; however that which Taz wrote plainly that the Haggadah is an interruption — one can explain: behold in siman 475 Beit Yosef at the beginning of the siman brought in the name of Mordechai that if from the outset he intended for this and did not divert his attention, he is permitted; Magen Avraham brought it there sign 1 and explains that which is written in the Gemara "perhaps diverting attention" means without intention, but if he intended for this and did not divert attention it is fine; if so, why is it different on Pesach from all days of the year — behold there is a remedy as written, and Eliyah Rabbah 475 and see there it will be explained. And see Levush in seif 1: he wrote if he washes before Kiddush he will need at the first dipping to wash and bless, and the second berachah will be in vain, see there; and he follows his view in seif 6 that even on other days of the year one does not bless al netilat yadayim for dipping in liquid; on Pesach one blesses al netilat yadayim for dipping in liquid (and the custom is not so even on Pesach, see below); and if so one should explain Mordechai thus, and N'tziv's question is not difficult either; and for the halachah: if he washed hands before Kiddush and blessed al netilat yadayim, it is obvious — whoever did not divert his attention during the Haggadah and did not touch an unclean place, it is forbidden to bless again al netilat yadayim for HaMotzi; and as a mere stringency he should wash hands for HaMotzi without berachah al netilat yadayim, for in the Gemara it says that according to one opinion "diverting," etc.; and see siman 158 seif 7 in the Hagah and Taz there sign 11, that even when he washed hands for dipping in liquid and did not bless al netilat yadayim and did not intend that this washing should count for HaMotzi, nevertheless he should not bless afterward al netilat yadayim for HaMotzi as long as he did not divert his attention; and if so it is fitting for everyone when he washes hands for dipping 1 that he should intend explicitly not to fulfill with this washing for HaMotzi; and proof from what Rashal wrote Yoreh De'ah siman 3: even though non-sacred meat does not require intention, nevertheless if he intended to gouge and uproot the opposite of the intention, it is invalid — the same here; and see 198 siman 61 in niddah who went down to inspect: it appears at first glance that even intention not for immersion but only to inspect, immersion applies to her; and if so it is better that before HaMotzi he bring himself to obligation of washing by pouring on his feet or foot-water and rubbing, and bless al netilat yadayim, for whoever acts out of doubt does not bless a berachah that is not needed, and Eliyah Rabbah; and Magen Avraham 3 and Eliyah Rabbah there will explain further on this, see there:
peri-megadim/2:א: (א) And he does not Taz: and for the first three cups b'dieved it suffices with the majority of a revi'it that he drinks his full mouthfuls; and a cup of revi'it requires that he drink a full revi'it in order to bless the blessing acharonah — see siman 190 in Taz 3 and 486 1:
peri-megadim/2:ב: (ב) See in Tur what the Rosh wrote: even if he diverted his attention from drinking, he drinks between the first two cups and it does not appear as adding to the cups — even a berachah is difficult from what the Rosh wrote. In Pesachim 108a between 3 and 4 it appears as adding, for according to him there is no distinction between berachah or not — Magen Avraham 472 sign 4; and some write that it is forbidden to drink between 3 and 4 and also after 4 from custom — see siman 481; it would be for the Rosh to omit this reason, which is the main one. And Bach explained that even for the Rosh, whatever he says in a berachah is adding, and without berachah and without Haggadah it is not adding — if so, it requires study:
peri-megadim/3:_: Or Taz: and see siman 321 seif 2 that two-thirds salt and one-third water — even a little is forbidden; and Taz there 6 and Magen Avraham here 5 and Eliyah Rabbah there will be explained:
peri-megadim/4:_: They are accustomed Taz: meat to roast on coals as a remembrance of the Pesach on a pomegranate spit; and because of the trouble they roast on coals, for also the Pesach if roasted on coals is fine — Eshel Avraham 5:280 chapter 8 halachah 10, Magen Avraham 8. And that which Taz wrote that one should not eat the meat on the first night — Pri Chadash agreed; and even if the meat is cooked, as long as it is a remembrance of the Pesach one does not eat on the first night except tomorrow if he wishes; and the egg is permitted to eat at night, for not only on account of remembrance of the festival offering do they cook an egg — there is also a reason of remembrance of mourning; and thereby he gave a reason for what the Mechaber wrote (Tur Rama): meat they roast and the egg they cook, because they are accustomed to eat the egg at night; if so, also fish and egg have no prohibition of roasted, as siman 476 seif 6; nevertheless they instituted on erev Yom Tov to cook the egg as well. And one can say for us: the festival offering of the 14th is optional and eaten cooked like all peace-offerings — Eshel Avraham 5:280 chapter 8 halachah 12 and Pesachim 70a; if so, the custom to cook the egg is a remembrance of the festival offering, etc. However Mishna Berurah wrote that they are accustomed to roast also the egg and one is permitted to eat the egg at night even roasted; but the meat, even cooked, they do not eat at night except by day tomorrow — see Eliyah Rabbah 86 seif 5: if they cooked a non-kosher egg with kosher eggs, see there; and wheat among them — 51 in Pesach forbids even m'b'eod yom until night if there are not sixty against the wheat, and if they are not peeled they are forbidden — see there Taz 10 and Shach 15:
peri-megadim/5:_: But Taz and Magen Avraham: maratich is (chrain); also what is beneath the ground comes out; and root means the small ones — see there:
peri-megadim/6:_: He washes Taz: and see siman 158 seif 2 and Eliyah Rabbah there, and he explains well sign 11 in the name of Mateh Yosef who was very strict. But one does not bless al netilat yadayim on something whose dipping is in liquid, even on the night of Pesach — and see Levush here and Eliyah Rabbah in 158. And know that there are three reasons: (1) on account of residue of terumah, and this is the opinion of Rashi z"l — even though for fruits 43, nevertheless liquids are prone [to contract impurity] and become primary; they decreed more stringently; and therefore even a moist liquid also requires washing. And Tosafot Pesachim 116a s.v. kol: the reason is that it is forbidden to defile one's body; and therefore specifically when there is in the liquids a revi'it, the measure of defiling the body — Eshel Avraham, Taz chapter 4 halachah 2; and possibly the Sages did not distinguish. And Beit Yosef Orach Chaim 164 in the name of R' Yehudah: the reason is on account of cleanliness — Taz there sign 6; and in Sefer Rosh Yosef in Chullin we wrote: one who dips a radish in salt and it becomes water and dissolves — one can say its dipping is in liquid — Magen Avraham 462:7 and Kaf HaChayim seif 12 and Rambam z"l chapter 8 halachah 49. And see Darkei Moshe in 158: plum juice, since it changed, they bless Borei peri ha'eitz — it is not "something whose dipping is in liquid," and it requires study whether we say that for impurity it is a liquid, and likewise honey-water and beer of this kind; and that which Tosafot wrote that it is forbidden to defile one's body — one can see in Chullin 44 that it appears only a kohen is warned, and rabbinically from the Torah only for impurity of the dead, but an Israelite is not warned — see Chochmas Adam in four views. And Magen Avraham 489:4 — and it is simple that a kohen is warned rabbinically in the time of the Temple not to defile his body; nevertheless it is a mixture that is visible to Israelites. And behold on the night of Pesach, which implies in Levush that they bless al netilat yadayim for dipping in liquid — one can say that on the festival all Israelites are warned to purify themselves; and it is fine to say they are careful specifically on Yom Tov, and the same on every Yom Tov. Butter — Taz 164:9 and Magen Avraham 7, and so 81 and 89 from Taz: curdled milk — if we say it is not a liquid, butter too even though it dissolved. See in Pri Megadim in siman 158, see there:
peri-megadim/7:_: And not Taz. And we already wrote in the previous sign that one can say on Yom Tov a person is obligated to purify himself — they are more careful. That which is written in Teshuvat She'elah to a girl — according to Rashi and Rashbam z"l, and Eliyah Rabbah explained: (1) the way of freedom — they dip before the meal to extend appetite for food. (2) They need to say the Haggadah and tell of the Exodus from Egypt; therefore they dip before eating without lingering, likewise without eating. (3) The children will ask about the second dipping: why — did they not already dip in the first? And the answer: dipping 1 is as all year, and dipping 2 is on account of the mitzvah of maror. And Taz explained that the question is on dipping 1 and the answer is to instruct about dipping 2; just as the first is not for the need of the meal, so the second only on account of the mitzvah of maror — a rabbinic mitzvah, for dipping is certainly only d'rabbanan, and maror too in our time — Magen Avraham and Eliyah Rabbah there will be explained. And see siman 475, see further in sign 8 of this:
